_comment: The source registry for NYC. One entry per source, each naming an adapter.
MVP = tier 2 only (NYC Open Data). Tier 0 aggregators (PredictHQ, SeatGeek)
and tier 1 venue adapters need keys or bespoke parsers; see coverage.md.
Datasets audited 2026-08-01. fudw-fgrp (Parks Events Listing) and
6v4b-5gp4 (Parks Special Events) are DEAD -- their newest rows are from
2019 -- and are deliberately absent rather than silently returning nothing.

sources.label: NYC Parks Public Events - Upcoming 14 Days
Squarespace venue calendars
_comment: Venue-published events, one collection per venue. The registry of
venue -> collection URL is discovered by squarespace.py and committed;
this adapter only fetches. Re-run discovery when venues redesign, not
on every run. Events live in the response's `upcoming` array -- for an
events collection `items` comes back empty, which is the whole trick.

sources.label: Luma community calendars
_comment: Organiser-led programming -- meetups, run clubs, reading and craft
groups -- which appears in no other source here. Each calendar
publishes a real ICS feed at api.lu.ma/ics/get, the Subscribe
button's own endpoint; this is a feed used as a feed, not a scrape.
Discovery is the limit, not access: there is no city-wide feed and
the /nyc page yields 20 calendars per load, so luma.py MERGES its
registry on each run and the roster grows over time.

sources.label: Ticketmaster Discovery
_comment: DMA 345 is the New York media market, which reaches Newark, Long
Island and lower Connecticut. state_code trims the other states at
the API; normalize.py then drops anything whose venue coordinates
fall outside an NYC neighbourhood polygon, which is the real test.
Sharded one day per request: deep paging caps at 1000 items and the
market holds ~4,600 events per month, so a single broad query would
silently see only a fifth of them.
Key lives in .env as TICKETMASTER_API_KEY (gitignored).

sources.label: DICE
_comment: Independent music and nightlife -- the venue tier that sells through
neither Ticketmaster nor a Squarespace calendar, and which the index
was missing entirely. DICE publishes sitemaps, marks every event page
up as schema.org, and its robots.txt says `Allow: /`. This reads the
surfaces a site provides in order to be indexed.
Its content signal is `search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference`, so the
adapter keeps a short listing and links back to DICE rather than
mirroring the page -- that is why normalize.py cuts the description
to a single line, and not merely for tidiness.
city_slugs are the `-<city>-tickets` slug suffixes that mean this
city. new-york and brooklyn are separate because DICE labels them
separately; bare `york` is deliberately absent, because 53 of those
are a venue in York, England. The suffix is only a prefilter -- each
event's own coordinates decide whether it is really in the city.
horizon_days is 60 rather than Ticketmaster's 30. The sitemap is
fetched whole either way, and lastmod means a wider window costs
almost nothing on a second run.

sources.label: Brooklyn Public Library
_comment: A completely open Drupal JSON:API -- no key, server-side date
filtering, cursor pagination, and every branch in the borough behind
one endpoint. The largest institutional source found: library
programming appears in no other feed here and is exactly the tier the
coverage thesis is about.
`field_date.value` arrives as `...T10:00:00+00:00` for an event the
site's own slug calls `1000am`. It is a naive local time wearing a UTC
offset, and fetch.py drops that offset deliberately -- honouring it
moves every story time to 6am. See fetch_drupal's docstring.
`field_event_type_parent` is the OPERATIONAL classification: Program,
Meeting Room, In-Branch Tabling, Outreach, Visit. Only some of those
are public events, which is the permitted-events lesson again -- an
internal room booking is not a listing. normalize.py rejects the rest.
Do NOT filter on `field_event_ptype`: it is null on every upcoming
row. `field_tags` is the live vocabulary and is what classifies these.

sources.label: WordPress venue calendars
_comment: Venue-published events from The Events Calendar, by whichever route
each venue answers on: its REST API where that is enabled, its ICS
export otherwise. posttypes.py discovers the registry and commits it;
this only subscribes.
This source exists because the earlier conclusion was wrong. `Tribe
REST is not the backbone -- 0/10` was measured against ten venues that
did not run the plugin. Of the census sites that do, most serve the
REST API and most serve a working ICS. Only venues that actually
returned something are registered -- an endpoint answering with
nothing is what made the earlier ICS sweep look like a 3% format.
Coordinates come from the OSM record rather than the feed: Tribe's
venue object is empty on most of these sites, and the census swept a
bounding box that includes Hoboken, Newark and the Meadowlands.
